To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the Görtler vortex mechanism is not operational in the boundary layer on swept walls of variable curvature for sufficiently large crossflow velocities.

(i) the most unstable mode for a swept concave wall is time-dependent for small values of crossflow velocity; (ii) for larger values of crossflow, the most unstable eigenfunctions become centre modes of the Orr–Sommerrfeld equation; (iii) the critical Görtler numbers for these modes are much smaller than the two-dimensional values; (iv) for order unity values for the ratio of crossflow to chordwise velocity, the Görtier instability is not operational
the Görtler vortex mechanism is not operational when the ratio of the maximum crossflow and chordflow velocity components is order unity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the stability of a three-dimensional boundary layer on an infinitely long concave wall of variable curvature.
the effect of the crossflow on the stability characteristics of boundary layers.
the linear stability of a boundary layer on a swept wall.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Görtler vortices are only a possibility in a three-dimensional boundary layer and not a certainty.
for order unity crossflow velocities and chordwise Reynolds numbers, the Görtlet instability mechanism is not operational.

the Görtler vortex mechanism is operational in the boundary layer on a swept wing only for very small values of the relative crossflow velocity field and that for all realistic values of the cross flow, other instability mechanisms are more likely to be operational.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the three-dimensional boundary-layer flow on a concave swept wall is centrifugaly unstable for sufficiently high Görtler numbers and that this instability is most pronounced when the crossflow is of order O(Re–1).
the Görtler mechanism is only operational for small crossflow and small curvature effects.
the Görtler mechanism is only effective when the crossflow is small compared to the chordwise flow.
The main takeaway from our work is that

in three dimensions, Görtler instabilities are not necessarily the result of centrifugal instability, but rather the result of a complex interplay between centrifugal effects, pressure gradients, and crossflow.
the Görtler vortex mechanism is not operational when the crossflow velocity in the boundary layer is comparable with the chordwise velocity.
the Görtler vortex mechanism is unlikely to be operational in most situations of engineering interest.
